learn.hook: Leave a potato in a dark corner for a few weeks and tiny shoots pop out of its 'eyes'. Plant it, and you get new potato plants without any seeds at all!
points: Reproduction is the making of new individuals of the same kind. In asexual reproduction a single parent produces offspring, without gametes.
Fission: Amoeba and bacteria split into two (binary fission); the malaria parasite Plasmodium splits into many at once (multiple fission).

Budding: a small outgrowth (bud) grows on the parent and develops into a new individual, as in Hydra and yeast. Fragmentation: a filament of Spirogyra breaks into pieces and each piece grows into a new one. Regeneration: a cut piece of Planaria can grow into a whole new animal.
Spore formation: bread mould (Rhizopus) makes spores in sporangia, which grow into new moulds in moist, warm places.

Vegetative propagation: new plants grow from roots, stems or leaves, such as potato eyes, ginger rhizomes, onion bulbs, Bryophyllum leaf buds and rose stem cuttings. Offspring of asexual reproduction are nearly identical to the parent.

example.q: Think it through: A farmer wants all his new mango trees to give fruit exactly as sweet as his best tree. Should he grow them from seeds or by grafting? Why?
steps: Seeds come from sexual reproduction and combine traits from two parents.
So trees from seeds may give fruit that is different from the parent tree.
Grafting is vegetative propagation, a form of asexual reproduction.
Grafted trees carry the same traits as the parent, so the fruit will be the same.
example.answer: Grafting, because asexually produced plants are nearly identical to the parent.

learn.reallife: Nurseries grow roses from cuttings and mangoes by grafting, and farmers plant sugarcane from stem pieces instead of seeds.

games.title: Match the organism to its method
Asexual reproduction: true or false?
items: Asexual reproduction needs only one parent
No gametes from two parents are needed.
A potato is a modified root
A potato is a stem tuber; its 'eyes' are buds.
Offspring from asexual reproduction are nearly identical to the parent
They get their genetic material from one parent only.
A bud grows on the side of Hydra and breaks off as a new Hydra.
Bread mould spreads by making seeds

quiz.q: How does Amoeba usually reproduce?
quiz.explain: A full-grown Amoeba divides its nucleus and then its cytoplasm to form two daughter cells.
quiz.mistake: Confuses splitting into two with budding

quiz.q: Which of these reproduces by budding?
quiz.explain: In yeast a small bud grows out from the parent cell and separates to live on its own.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up budding with fragmentation or spore formation

quiz.q: New Bryophyllum plants grow from
options: buds on the margins of its leaves
quiz.explain: Bryophyllum (patharchatta) has buds along the notches of its leaf margins that grow into new plants.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all new plants must come from seeds

quiz.q: A filament of Spirogyra breaks into small pieces and each piece grows into a new filament. This is
quiz.explain: In fragmentation the body simply breaks into pieces, and each piece grows into a new individual.
quiz.mistake: Confuses fragmentation with regeneration, where specialised cells rebuild lost parts

quiz.q: Bread mould (Rhizopus) spreads to new slices of bread by
quiz.explain: Rhizopus produces tiny spores in round sporangia. The spores travel through the air and grow on moist food.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fungi make seeds like plants

quiz.q: Which part of a potato grows into a new plant?
quiz.explain: A potato is an underground stem (tuber). Its 'eyes' are buds that sprout into new shoots.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that the eyes of a potato are buds

quiz.q: The malaria parasite Plasmodium divides into many daughter cells at the same time. This is called
quiz.explain: In multiple fission, one cell divides into many daughter cells at once.
quiz.mistake: Thinks fission always produces just two cells

quiz.q: What is a disadvantage of asexual reproduction for a species?
options: There is very little variation among offspring
quiz.explain: Asexual offspring are nearly identical, so if the environment changes, they may all be affected in the same way.
quiz.mistake: Thinks asexual reproduction is slow, when it is usually fast

teach.ask: Gappu finds a sprouting potato: "There are no seeds here! How can a potato make new plants?"
teach.praise: Chirp! The potato's eyes are buds on an underground stem. This is vegetative propagation, a kind of asexual reproduction, so the new plants are just like the parent!
teach.nudge: Which part of the potato actually sprouts? What are those little 'eyes'?

learn.hook: A bee buzzing from one sunflower to another is doing an important job without knowing it: helping the plants make seeds!
points: The flower is the reproductive part of a flowering plant. The stamen is the male part: an anther (which makes pollen grains) on a filament. The pistil (carpel) is the female part: stigma, style and ovary, which contains ovules.

Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma. Self-pollination happens within the same flower or plant; cross-pollination happens between flowers of different plants of the same kind.
Pollen is carried by wind, water, insects and birds. Bright, scented flowers with nectar usually attract insects; wind-pollinated flowers make large amounts of light pollen.
Fertilisation: a pollen tube grows from the pollen grain down the style into the ovule, and a male gamete fuses with the female gamete (egg) to form a zygote.
After fertilisation, the zygote grows into an embryo, the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit. Petals and stamens usually wither and fall.

example.q: Think it through: A mango flower has been pollinated and fertilised. What will each part become?
steps: Inside the ovule, the zygote divides to form the embryo, the baby plant.
The ovule develops into the seed (the guthli) with the embryo inside.
The ovary swells and ripens into the fruit, the juicy mango.
The petals and stamens dry up and fall off.
example.answer: Zygote → embryo, ovule → seed, ovary → fruit.

learn.reallife: Farmers keep bee boxes near mustard and sunflower fields because bees improve pollination and the harvest of seeds.

games.title: Male or female part of the flower?
From flower to fruit
items: A pollen tube grows down the style to the ovule
Male gamete fuses with the egg (fertilisation)
Ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit

quiz.q: What is the male reproductive part of a flower called?
quiz.explain: The stamen, made of an anther and a filament, is the male part. It produces pollen.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up stamen (male) and pistil (female)

quiz.q: Where are pollen grains produced?
quiz.explain: The anther, at the top of the stamen, makes pollen grains, which contain the male gametes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks pollen is made in the female part

quiz.q: What is pollination?
options: Fusion of male and female gametes
Growth of a seed into a plant
Transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma
quiz.explain: Pollination only moves pollen to the stigma. Fertilisation, the fusion of gametes, happens later.
quiz.mistake: Uses pollination and fertilisation as if they mean the same

quiz.q: Pollen from a flower on one mustard plant reaches the stigma of a flower on another mustard plant. This is
quiz.explain: Cross-pollination is the transfer of pollen between flowers on different plants of the same kind.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any pollination by insects is self-pollination

quiz.q: After fertilisation, the ovary of a flower develops into the
quiz.explain: The ovary swells and ripens into the fruit, which protects the seeds.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the ovary (becomes fruit) with the ovule (becomes seed)

quiz.q: After fertilisation, the ovule develops into the
quiz.explain: Each fertilised ovule becomes a seed containing the embryo.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the ovule with the ovary

quiz.q: Inside the ovule, the zygote develops into the
quiz.explain: The zygote divides many times to form the embryo, which can later grow into a new plant.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what the zygote becomes

quiz.q: A flower is brightly coloured, sweet-smelling and full of nectar. How is it most likely pollinated?
quiz.explain: Colour, scent and nectar attract insects such as bees and butterflies, which carry pollen from flower to flower.
quiz.mistake: Does not link flower features with the pollinating agent

teach.ask: Gappu sees a bee covered in yellow dust: "Why is the bee so dusty? And how does a flower turn into a fruit with seeds?"
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! The bee carries pollen to the stigma (pollination), then gametes fuse (fertilisation), the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes the fruit!
teach.nudge: Once the pollen reaches the stigma, what has to happen before a seed can form?

learn.hook: Every frog, every peacock and every person began life as a single tiny cell. How can one cell grow into a whole animal?
points: In sexual reproduction two parents produce gametes: the male gamete is the sperm and the female gamete is the egg (ovum). Their fusion is called fertilisation.
Fertilisation forms a single cell, the zygote. It divides again and again to form an embryo, which grows into a new individual.
Internal fertilisation happens inside the female's body, as in humans, cows, dogs and hens. External fertilisation happens outside, usually in water, as in frogs and most fish.
Animals that give birth to young ones are viviparous (humans, cows, dogs). Animals that lay eggs are oviparous (hens, frogs, turtles). In humans, the embryo develops inside the mother's uterus.

Some animals change form as they grow, called metamorphosis: a frog goes from egg to tadpole to adult. Sexual reproduction mixes features of two parents, which gives variation and helps a species survive changes.

example.q: Think it through: Frogs lay hundreds of eggs, but a cow usually gives birth to only one calf at a time. Why might frogs need so many eggs?
steps: Frogs have external fertilisation in water.
Many eggs and sperm are carried away by water, eaten or never meet.
The eggs and tadpoles are not protected inside the mother's body.
So frogs lay many eggs to make sure that at least some survive to become adults.
example.answer: With external fertilisation and no protection inside the body, many eggs are lost, so frogs lay large numbers.

learn.reallife: India is one of the world's major silk producers, and silk farmers (sericulturists) rear silkworms through their life cycle of egg, larva, pupa and moth.

games.title: Life cycle of a frog
games.prompt: Arrange the stages from first to last
items: Tadpole hatches and breathes through gills
Tail shrinks and the young frog leaves the water

quiz.q: What is the fusion of a male gamete and a female gamete called?
quiz.explain: Fertilisation is the fusion of the sperm and the egg to form a zygote.
quiz.mistake: Confuses fertilisation with pollination, which happens only in plants

quiz.q: What is the single cell formed by fertilisation called?
quiz.explain: The zygote is the first cell of the new individual. It later divides to form the embryo.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the zygote with the embryo, which forms after many cell divisions

quiz.q: In frogs, where does fertilisation take place?
quiz.explain: Female frogs lay eggs in water and the male releases sperm over them, so fertilisation is external.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all animals have internal fertilisation

quiz.q: A hen lays eggs, and fertilisation happens inside her body. Which describes a hen?
quiz.explain: In hens, fertilisation is internal, and the hen then lays eggs, so she is oviparous.
quiz.mistake: Thinks animals that lay eggs must have external fertilisation

quiz.q: Which of these animals is viviparous?
quiz.explain: A cow gives birth to a calf, so it is viviparous. Frogs, hens and crocodiles lay eggs.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up oviparous and viviparous

quiz.q: A tadpole is a stage in the life cycle of which animal?
quiz.explain: A frog's egg hatches into a tadpole, which changes into an adult frog through metamorphosis.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the tadpole with the larva of an insect

quiz.q: In the life cycle of a silkworm, which stage lives inside the silk cocoon?
quiz.explain: The silkworm caterpillar (larva) spins a silk cocoon around itself and becomes a pupa inside it.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the order egg, larva, pupa, adult in a silkworm

quiz.q: What is a main advantage of sexual reproduction?
options: Offspring are exact copies of a parent
It is always faster than asexual reproduction
quiz.explain: Offspring get features from two parents, so they differ from each other. Variation helps a species survive when conditions change.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the features of sexual and asexual reproduction

teach.ask: Gappu looks at his own egg shell: "I came out of an egg, but puppies don't! How do animals make babies?"
teach.praise: Chirp! A sperm and an egg fuse in fertilisation to form a zygote that grows into a baby. Birds like me are oviparous, and puppies are born because dogs are viviparous!
teach.nudge: What has to happen between the two gametes before a baby animal can start growing?
